idea.value: A teaser that never shows the product: it argues that an idea is not real until it can be seen and measured, by setting a short spoken sentence as tiny centred captions over macro footage that is constantly being annotated, measured and re-graded.
evidence: speech-text.json screenText: five sentence-case captions of two to five words at 0.133, 2.067, 3.533, 5.133 and 7.333 s, read as one argument: an obvious claim, then an idea nobody understands yet

audience.value: Design and product people who already know the maker's world (studio, tooling or hardware brand followers): no product, no logo, no call to action is shown, so it assumes the viewer will look the brand up or already follows it.
evidence: visuals/a1/w-k.jpg F220-F259: the film ends on the caption and black, no mark

value.device: frame strobe plus a statement caption
value.description: F0-F8 a dot-matrix ring strobes against black frame by frame with stray blue bars, and the 2-word caption is already on screen at F4 (0.133 s). F9 (0.300) is a full white frame that grades down into a macro eye with measurement boxes drawing on (F10-F13). The eye reads before the brain parses the caption, and the HUD says 'this is being measured' before anything is explained.

value.purpose: Hook: a claim of certainty set against an image under analysis
value.retentionDevice: frame-level strobe, then a white flash resolving into an eye
value.content: dot-ring strobe, eye plate with HUD boxes, first caption held 30 frames

value.purpose: Breath: two long macro holds in near-silence that set the place
value.retentionDevice: slow push and slow roll, grade steps at the hand-off between plates
value.content: light crescent on a dark sphere (44 frames, 7% push), pen nib drawing a line (28 frames, 2.8 degree roll); second caption on the crescent only

value.purpose: Turn: the montage shows what the idea could be, too fast to hold
value.retentionDevice: a 9-frame lead plate, ten 4-frame plates and a 6-frame plate; one caption over the first six, then the next caption then the caption changes over a drawing that measures itself
value.content: dark objects, a dome, sparks, the eye again, wireframe, glass dome, particles, a hand typing, a droplet, scattered digits, a technical drawing with a counting degree readout

value.purpose: Payoff: the picture empties while the sentence completes
value.retentionDevice: ground swaps on a held caption, a blinking caret, a deleted line, four empty frames, the last line held 34 frames
value.content: ultramarine then navy card, black ground with a glowing caret, closing caption, 6 black frames

payoff.value: The sentence resolves on an empty black frame: the last line holds 34 frames (7.333-8.467 s) with nothing else in picture, so the line itself is the 'idea' the film has been building toward.

callToAction.value: None on screen. The film ends on 6 frames of black (F254-F259) under loud sound; any brand mark must come from a following card or the post that carries it.

whyItWorks: The caption is the only constant: always centred, always about 3% cap height, white. The eye parks on it while plates, grades and grounds change underneath, so even 4-frame plates read as one thought.

Speed is used once. The 1.83 s burst of 4-frame plates (3.533-5.367) is framed by two long holds before (1.47 s and 0.93 s) and a 3.3 s near-empty ending after, so it reads as a surge rather than noise.
Annotation sells 'technology' without showing a product: HUD boxes with pixel dimensions on the eye, a degree readout counting 170.4 to 172.1 on the drawing.
Every plate is touched by the grade: white-out, magenta, teal, monochrome, negative, cream. The grade steps are the film's transitions, so the footage feels authored rather than stock.
The ending subtracts: the picture goes from footage to flat colour to black with a caret, and the line is deleted and replaced, which stages the sentence's own claim that the idea is unfinished.
